raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add an opt-in custom scheduler example that adjusts the total per-step token
budget under mixed prefill/decode load. It uses the existing `scheduler_cls`
extension point and leaves the standard scheduler and defaults unchanged.
Related discussion: [P-PAS RFC #52906](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52906).

## Claims

- Provide a bounded, configurable example with pressure thresholds, minimum
  residence and a rate-limited budget boost for stalled prefills.
- Preserve native allocation, request order and lifecycle; restore the configured
  capacity after each scheduling call. Reject unsupported configurations.
- Document the trade-offs and exercise the example through the existing plugin
  test suite, including actual model generation with prefix caching on and off.

## Validation

Base: `e9acf48614a2c0d027d7aa2f0e38d963117617a6`. Hardware: one RTX 5090, 32 GB.
Model: Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B, BF16. On this main commit, all 16 added tests passed
(60.62 s, four fork deprecation warnings; the existing OPT dummy test was
deselected). This includes both GPU generation cases using Model Runner V2,
PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130 and official precompiled extensions from `49d634bd6`;
native sources, build configuration and dependencies are unchanged between the
two commits. The same tests also passed on that original base. Local model
redirect and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` were used. Exact commands, environment pins
and raw logs accompany the revision report linked below.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/plugins_tests/test_scheduler_plugins.py -k adaptive_budget -v
pre-commit run --files \
  examples/features/adaptive_budget/scheduler.py \
  tests/plugins_tests/test_scheduler_plugins.py tests/v1/core/utils.py \
  docs/features/adaptive_budget.md docs/features/README.md \
  .buildkite/test_areas/plugins.yaml
```

The external experiment suite passes 54 tests on vLLM 0.22.1, including real
allocator lifecycle tests and 4×1000 controller differential steps. The full
pre-commit command passed on the submission base: 17 applicable checks passed,
and 19 had no matching files. No SKIP override was used. An earlier Go-download
TLS failure was resolved by installing a checksum-verified official toolchain.
Hosted CI has not yet run.

Exploratory serving measurements used vLLM 0.22.1, three seeds, randomized
policy order, 30 runs and 1440 requests with zero failures. The adaptive arm ran
this example. Runner capacity was held at 8192 tokens, max sequences 64, with
chunked prefill, CUDA graphs, and prefix caching/tracing disabled.
These are not current-main performance measurements.
Client timing included 1220 multi-token SSE chunks; tokens in such a chunk share
a timestamp, so these interarrival measurements have limited time resolution.

| Burst workload | Native 8192 | Fixed runtime 1024 | Adaptive |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 715.67 | 987.94 | 882.20 |
| P99 client token interarrival (ms) | 150.08 | 42.22 | 45.14 |
| Mean end-to-end latency (ms) | 3237.28 | 3650.95 | 3508.79 |
| Output tokens/s | 651.50 | 637.12 | 641.99 |

The three-seed paired ITL reduction versus native was 69.27–70.95%, with
7.95–8.63% worse end-to-end latency and 1.31–1.55% lower throughput. Relative
to fixed 1024, end-to-end latency improved 3.49–4.23% while ITL worsened
3.31–9.51%. Steady traffic was approximately unchanged from native. This is a
trade-off, not a universal speedup; three seeds do not establish significance.

Generation checks use the existing `check_logprobs_close` helper. Batch-shape
changes can alter greedy outputs: the separate experiment observed 2/3 exact
outputs without prefix caching and 6/6 with it; native fixed-capacity 128 also
produced the short-output divergence. At the first divergence the winning tokens
were mutually in the other run's top-5. This criterion does not establish full
sequence or probability equality.

Full evidence: [revision report](https://github.com/codegx686/vllm/blob/adaptive-budget-evidence-20261024/REVISION_REPORT.md),
[raw measurements and per-seed comparisons](https://github.com/codegx686/vllm/tree/adaptive-budget-evidence-20261024/results/revision-20261024),
[validation logs](https://github.com/codegx686/vllm/tree/adaptive-budget-evidence-20261024/logs),
and [source/evidence hashes](https://github.com/codegx686/vllm/blob/adaptive-budget-evidence-20261024/DELIVERY_MANIFEST.json).

## Details

The example scans runnable requests once per iteration and temporarily narrows
`max_num_scheduled_tokens`, restoring capacity in `finally`. Prefill replay after
preemption is included; request identity prevents reused IDs from inheriting a
previous request's progress timer. The native scheduler still owns allocation,
preemption and cancellation. No GPU synchronization is added.

Scope is synchronous, single-GPU text generation with chunked prefill. A boost
provides a progress opportunity rather than a starvation bound. Smaller total
budgets can delay decodes and worsen TTFT; queue scanning has linear CPU cost.
This relies on the concrete Scheduler implementation and must be checked on
upgrades. Documentation covers configuration, limitations and evaluation.

Unlike P-PAS's aggregate **prefill** cap, this example caps **all** scheduled
tokens. It is not a P-PAS implementation or reproduction. The existing plugin
Buildkite step already runs this test module; source dependencies are extended
to select it when the example or scheduler changes. Hosted CI and AMD validation
remain to be run. AI assistance was used to implement, review and validate this
contribution. The human submitter has reviewed the changes, confirmed the
relevant tests and approved DCO sign-off.

The 2026-10-24 duplicate-work search also checked EWSJF #33392, FlowPrefill
#44794 and long-prefill defer #61080. Those use different queue, chunk-execution
or defer mechanisms; no equivalent open custom-scheduler example was found.
The refreshed search evidence and RFC discussion are included in the report
bundle. Maintainer agreement on accepting this example is still needed.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

</details>

+# Adaptive token budgets (scheduler example)
+
+The [adaptive budget example](../../examples/features/adaptive_budget/scheduler.py)
+uses `scheduler_cls` to vary the total number of tokens scheduled per iteration.
+It is opt-in: the standard scheduler and its defaults are unchanged. This is a
+reference extension for experimenting with the latency/throughput trade-off,
+not a universally faster scheduling policy.
+
+## Run the example
+
+From a vLLM source checkout, make the example importable in the engine process:
+
+```bash
+PYTHONPATH="$PWD${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}" vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B \
+    --scheduler-cls examples.features.adaptive_budget.scheduler.AdaptiveBudgetScheduler \
+    --no-async-scheduling --enable-chunked-prefill \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
+    --additional-config '{"adaptive_budget":{"high_budget":8192,"low_budget":1024,"guard_budget":4096}}'
+```
+
+Synchronous scheduling and chunked prefill are required. Use a single GPU and
+a text-only decoder model. Speculative decoding, LoRA,
+pooling, encoder-decoder models, multimodal models, KV/encoder transfer and
+tensor/pipeline/data parallelism are rejected by this example. Prefix caching
+is allowed; a waiting request is conservatively counted as prefill until the
+native scheduler resolves its cache hit. Remove `--scheduler-cls` and the
+`adaptive_budget` entry to restore the standard scheduler.
+
+## Configuration and behavior
+
+All options below belong to `additional_config.adaptive_budget`.
+Unknown keys, nonintegral token budgets, and nonfinite timeouts are rejected.
+
+| Option | Default | Meaning |
+| --- | ---: | --- |
+| `high_budget` | 8192 | Open-state total token budget; must fit the configured scheduling capacity. |
+| `low_budget` | 1024 | Total token budget while mixed prefill/decode work is under pressure. |
+| `enter_prefills` | 2 | Enter the limited state at this number of runnable prefills with active decode. |
+| `exit_prefills` | 0 | Leave the limited state at or below this count; must be below `enter_prefills`. |
+| `min_dwell_steps` | 4 | Minimum steps between pressure transitions. |
+| `guard_enabled` | true | Allow a periodic budget boost after a prefill stops advancing. |
+| `max_stall_ms` | 250 | Monotonic elapsed time since the last observed computed-token increase. |
+| `guard_budget` | 4096 | Boosted budget; between `low_budget` and `high_budget`. |
+| `guard_interval_steps` | 8 | Minimum number of steps between boosts. |
+
+When either prefill or decode work disappears, the controller immediately
+returns to `high_budget`, bypassing minimum residence. With the default
+`exit_prefills=0`, this immediate-release rule handles exit; a positive exit
+threshold can also exit while mixed work remains. Recomputed generated tokens
+after preemption count as prefill work. Grammar/KV-blocked requests are excluded.
+
+The example delegates allocation, preemption, cancellation and request ordering
+to the native scheduler. It temporarily narrows `max_num_scheduled_tokens` and
+restores it in `finally`; it never resizes the model runner's compilation or
+buffer capacity. This relies on the concrete Scheduler implementation, so it
+must be checked when upgrading vLLM. It does not add GPU synchronization.
+
+A boost creates an opportunity for progress. It cannot guarantee admission or
+freedom from starvation: KV pressure and the native request order still apply.
+The observer scans the request map once per step, so CPU cost grows with queue
+depth. A smaller total budget may also delay decode requests, especially if it
+is smaller than the number of active sequences. Start with a low budget at least
+as large as `max_num_seqs` and measure the actual workload.
+
+## Evaluate the trade-off
+
+Compare against the standard scheduler, several fixed runtime budgets, and the
+existing `long_prefill_token_threshold` controls. Keep runner capacity, model,
+arrival traces, output lengths and warmup constant. Report TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end
+latency, throughput, failures and long/short request slices; record run-to-run
+variation. Smaller chunks can improve token interarrival latency while worsening
+TTFT and overall latency. Do not infer production gains from a single synthetic
+trace.
+
+The pressure predicate is inspired by [P-PAS RFC #52906](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52906).
+P-PAS caps aggregate **prefill** work while retaining the global token budget.
+This example caps **all** scheduled tokens and adds residence, hysteresis and a
+rate-limited progress boost. It is not an implementation or reproduction of
+P-PAS, and its results should not be labeled as P-PAS results.

@@ -0,0 +1,150 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""An opt-in example of bounded token budgets using the scheduler extension API."""
+
+import time
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator
+
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import SchedulerOutput
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler import Scheduler
+from vllm.v1.request import Request, RequestStatus
+
+
+class BudgetConfig(BaseModel):
+    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", strict=True, frozen=True)
+
+    high_budget: int = Field(default=8192, ge=1)
+    low_budget: int = Field(default=1024, ge=1)
+    enter_prefills: int = Field(default=2, ge=1)
+    exit_prefills: int = Field(default=0, ge=0)
+    min_dwell_steps: int = Field(default=4, ge=0)
+    guard_enabled: bool = True
+    max_stall_ms: float = Field(default=250.0, gt=0, allow_inf_nan=False)
+    guard_budget: int = Field(default=4096, ge=1)
+    guard_interval_steps: int = Field(default=8, ge=1)
+
+    @model_validator(mode="after")
+    def validate_bounds(self) -> "BudgetConfig":
+        if not self.low_budget <= self.guard_budget <= self.high_budget:
+            raise ValueError("Require low_budget <= guard_budget <= high_budget")
+        if self.exit_prefills >= self.enter_prefills:
+            raise ValueError("Require exit_prefills < enter_prefills")
+        return self
+
+
+class BudgetController:
+    """Select a total iteration budget without changing request order."""
+
+    def __init__(self, config: BudgetConfig):
+        self.config = config
+        self.limited = False
+        self.step = 0
+        self.last_switch = -config.min_dwell_steps
+        self.last_guard = -config.guard_interval_steps
+
+    def decide(self, prefills: int, decodes: int, stall_ms: float) -> int:
+        cfg = self.config
+        self.step += 1
+        previous = self.limited
+        if not prefills or not decodes:
+            self.limited = False
+        elif self.step - self.last_switch >= cfg.min_dwell_steps:
+            if not self.limited and prefills >= cfg.enter_prefills:
+                self.limited = True
+            elif self.limited and prefills <= cfg.exit_prefills:
+                self.limited = False
+        if previous != self.limited:
+            self.last_switch = self.step
+        if not self.limited:
+            return cfg.high_budget
+        if (
+            cfg.guard_enabled
+            and stall_ms >= cfg.max_stall_ms
+            and self.step - self.last_guard >= cfg.guard_interval_steps
+        ):
+            self.last_guard = self.step
+            return cfg.guard_budget
+        return cfg.low_budget
+
+
+class AdaptiveBudgetScheduler(Scheduler):
+    """Synchronous text-only example; the standard scheduler remains the default."""
+
+    def __init__(self, vllm_config: VllmConfig, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
+        sc = vllm_config.scheduler_config
+        if sc.async_scheduling or not sc.enable_chunked_prefill:
+            raise ValueError("Use synchronous scheduling with chunked prefill")
+        if (
+            sc.is_multimodal_model
+            or sc.runner_type != "generate"
+            or vllm_config.model_config.is_encoder_decoder
+            or vllm_config.speculative_config is not None
+            or vllm_config.lora_config is not None
+            or vllm_config.kv_transfer_config is not None
+            or vllm_config.ec_transfer_config is not None
+            or vllm_config.parallel_config.world_size != 1
+            or vllm_config.parallel_config.data_parallel_size != 1
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("This example requires single-GPU text generation")
+        additional = vllm_config.additional_config
+        if not isinstance(additional, dict):
+            raise ValueError("additional_config must be a dictionary")
+        self.budget_config = BudgetConfig.model_validate(
+            additional.get("adaptive_budget", {})
+        )
+        capacity = sc.max_num_scheduled_tokens or sc.max_num_batched_tokens
+        if self.budget_config.high_budget > capacity:
+            raise ValueError("high_budget exceeds the scheduler's configured capacity")
+        super().__init__(vllm_config, *args, **kwargs)
+        self.budget_controller = BudgetController(self.budget_config)
+        self.prefill_progress: dict[str, tuple[Request, int, float]] = {}
+
+    def _observe(self, now: float) -> tuple[int, int, float]:
+        prefills = decodes = 0
+        oldest_stall_ms = 0.0
+        live: set[str] = set()
+        for req_id, req in self.requests.items():
+            if req.status not in (
+                RequestStatus.WAITING,
+                RequestStatus.RUNNING,
+                RequestStatus.PREEMPTED,
+            ):
+                continue
+            # Replaying generated tokens after preemption is also prefill work.
+            prefill_end = max(req.num_prompt_tokens, req.num_tokens - 1)
+            if req.num_computed_tokens < prefill_end:
+                prefills += 1
+                live.add(req_id)
+                old_req, old_count, last_progress = self.prefill_progress.get(
+                    req_id, (req, req.num_computed_tokens, now)
+                )
+                if old_req is not req or req.num_computed_tokens > old_count:
+                    last_progress = now
+                self.prefill_progress[req_id] = (
+                    req,
+                    req.num_computed_tokens,
+                    last_progress,
+                )
+                oldest_stall_ms = max(oldest_stall_ms, (now - last_progress) * 1000)
+            elif req.status == RequestStatus.RUNNING:
+                decodes += 1
+        for req_id in self.prefill_progress.keys() - live:
+            del self.prefill_progress[req_id]
+        return prefills, decodes, oldest_stall_ms
+
+    def schedule(self, *args, **kwargs) -> SchedulerOutput:
+        budget = self.budget_controller.decide(*self._observe(time.monotonic()))
+        capacity = self.max_num_scheduled_tokens
+        self.max_num_scheduled_tokens = budget
+        try:
